lists.title: Things I refuse to pay full price for

entries.text: Digital artifacts like NFTs. A total scam.
Certain conceptual artwork like Comedian, the duct-taped banana. A bundle of fresh bananas from a supermarket taste just the same.
Various jewelries. They all look the same to me. Pick the cheapest if necessary.

versions.message: The consumer market is full of ridiculously priced products. If I have to choose, I prefer practicality to symbolism.

lists.title: Hills I'm 100% ready to die on

entries.text: Jesus claimed to be God, was crucified on the cross, defeated death and proved that he is God by resurrecting on the third day. I surrender myself to Jesus Christ my Lord and aspire to glorify our heavenly Father with the help of the Holy Spirit.

The most urgent problem humanity needs to solve collectively from now on, is the declining birthrate as societies develop. The society that doesn't revert this trend among its own population will either cease to exist or be replaced by population from other societies.
Apart from getting married and having children, my way of glorifying God is to become the godly man that inspires others to turn to Jesus Christ and bring the kingdom of heaven to earth together.

versions.message: These are not irrational convictions, but conclusions of mine after much contemplation and many trials and errors.

lists.title: Situations where I would ignore a phone call

entries.text: In the middle of a conversation with my family/friends, I will not look at the phone.
When I am at a live performance or a church service, I will not take out the phone.
When I am playing any sports, I usually put my phone away.

versions.message: Who still makes random phone calls nowadays? I keep the notifications on my phone at the minimum level. Except for direct messages, notifications of other apps are all silenced. I choose when to check them instead.

lists.title: Food I would eat off the floor

entries.text: BBQ lamb skewer with cumin and spice. It is never super hygiene to begin with, but the taste is worth all the risks.
Sizzling Sisig. This Filipino dish looks messy, but the taste is addictive.
Beef stake. I don't care how it's cooked. I'm not gonna leave it on the floor.

versions.message: Usually if I drop any food on the floor, I just pretend that my floor is quite clean, so I will pick up the food and eat it.

lists.title: Minor inconveniences that ruin my entire week

entries.text: One strand of stubborn facial hair that survived shaving. Once I notice it on my skin, I have to pull it out before I could focus on anything else.
A tiny scratch on a brand-new gadget I just bought. Especially if it's due to my own carelessness.
Forgot to complete a task squeezed into an errand as a bonus to-do item. What a wasted opportunity to be efficient!
An action or a remark of mine that didn't matter much at the time but was embarrassing in retrospect.

versions.message: No minor inconvenience really bothers me for as long as a week. But there are many regrets that I couldn't let go completely. That's for another list.

lists.title: Things I would save first in a house fire

entries.text: My order-made suits. If I'm going to be homeless, I'd prefer to be the sharpest looking of them all.
My snowboarding gears. If it's already winter, I would be shredding on the slopes and not staying at home anyways.
My laptop. It's all I need to start over, and I usually bring it with me anywhere I go.

versions.message: There is nothing in my house that holds sentimental value to me. Except for the obvious items such as legal documents and cash, there's nothing I would really rush to save in a house fire.
